legendEntries.label: Derived status axis — computed, never typed

nodes.label:
SODOTO Registry
SKILLS
nodes.note: v0.1 · 31 skills · 1 live credential. What a person can be certified in.  —  Already exists, dated 1 March 2026, on Models for Seeing Systems. Causal Loop Diagramming is Active — first mentor Kerry Turner, first credential Marc Pierson, 10 December 2025. The most developed of the three files, so it seeds the others rather than being replaced.

nodes.label:
methods.json
PATHWAYS
nodes.note: Ordered uses of tools. Each step carries question, gate and handoff; each method carries a fallback.  —  Sequence lives here and nowhere else, because a hammer is used in many processes and does a different job in each. Steps carry the question they answer, any gate that must hold first, and the handoff to the next step.

nodes.label:
catalog.json
TOOLS
nodes.note: id · what · shelf · status · launch · intro · manual · example · deck. What you can open.  —  No methods field. A tool cannot carry sequence. Shelving is a property here, not a folder on disk, because one tool sits on several shelves — the Graph Tool answers Why, How-strategy and How-mechanism.

nodes.label: CONFIDENCE
nodes.note: Values: two stars, one star, none, retired.  —  Derived from Do One and Teach One attestations on the method itself. Because a star is computed from signed credentials it cannot be talked up. Zero stars is a normal, publishable state.

nodes.label: TRANSMISSIBILITY
nodes.note: Values: Active, Ready, Candidate.  —  Marc's own axis, five months older than the star scheme. Read off whether the method's constituent skills have mentors and teaching chains. Orthogonal to confidence: a method can be proven and untransmissible, or teachable and untested.

nodes.label: Neo4j
nodes.note: Queries it makes cheap: derived back-links, impact analysis before a rename, gap-finding, path-finding, confidence, staleness.  —  If the database is down the storefront still works and the handout still opens. Nothing load-bearing sits only in the graph. Same arrangement as the SODOTO projector.

edges.label: REQUIRES_SKILL
edges.note: A method names the skills it requires; the registry certifies them. This is the join between the pathway layer and the person layer.

edges.label: USES
edges.note: Each step names one tool. The tool is the instrument, not the point — the step's question is the point.

edges.label: EMBODIES
edges.note: A tool that IS a method wearing a tool's clothes — A3 Problem Solving, the eVSM cycle. Build it as a tool, give it a method page, and have the two point at each other.

edges.label: Do One / Teach One
edges.note: A Do One earns the first star. A Teach One whose learner then runs it earns the second — the method crossed a person boundary, which is the real test.

edges.label: mentor + chain
edges.note: Active means at least one credential issued and the teaching chain begun. Ready means a mentor exists. Candidate means nominated, no mentor yet.

edges.label: marks
edges.note: Written onto the method as a computed field, never authored. If attestation is high-friction nobody logs runs, and untested becomes indistinguishable from unlogged — that is the risk that would kill the whole signal.

edges.label: marks
edges.note: Also computed. Together the two axes expose different failures, which is why collapsing them would hide exactly what each is built to reveal.
Skills and attestations become nodes and edges. The confidence query counts attestations by type and by NDC.
Pathways become ordered step chains. HANDS_OFF_TO edges are what a shortest-path query traverses.
Tools become nodes. 'What methods use this tool' stops being a script and becomes one hop.
